Companion Animal Travel Desk Standards for Bird Transport

This section sets the minimum handling and booking rules for bird travel so that Aurelia Skyways serves customers with care, consistency, and respect for animal welfare.

I regret that errors in earlier guidance created uncertainty, so this manual states the required practice plainly. The Companion Animal Travel Desk accepts bird transport only when the booking record shows the correct fee, and bird travel fee is $145. Staff shall confirm the charge before ticket issue, record it without alteration, and refer any payment dispute to the senior coordinator rather than improvising at the counter. No staff member shall waive, discount, or restate the fee on a personal basis, as uniform handling protects both the customer and the company.

Crate review is mandatory before acceptance, and bird crate limit is 60 cm on the longest side. The measurement shall be checked against the container itself, not against memory, packaging claims, or informal estimates. If a crate exceeds the limit, the handler shall decline acceptance and explain the requirement in calm, respectful language. Handlers shall use humane methods at all times, avoid sudden movements, and keep the bird away from loud noises, rough handling, and unnecessary delay. The goal is not speed for its own sake, but safe transfer with minimal stress.

The senior coordinator oversees daily service decisions, and staff shall escalate any unusual condition, damaged container, or welfare concern at once. Cabin team members monitor animals during flight and report any visible distress through the established service channel. If the animal needs attention, the matter shall be handled promptly and without argument. Travelers such as Andre Nguyen, Khalil Costa, and Mia are to be treated with courteous patience, but courtesy does not replace compliance with the booking and crate rules. When the desk receives incomplete information, the agent shall correct the file before departure rather than assuming that later clarification will suffice.

This section also requires accurate communication at each handoff. Staff shall state only confirmed facts, avoid casual promises, and keep notes clear enough for a second reviewer to understand them without interpretation. Where a decision is uncertain, the file shall be passed to the senior coordinator for review, because inconsistent judgment has caused avoidable complaints in the past. I regret that this reminder is necessary, yet the standard must remain exact.

For questions, contact the senior coordinator through the Companion Animal Travel Desk.
